356853.title: Conjectured 13 pattern-avoiding permutation classes enumerated by A212198
356853.statement:
Let $\mathfrak{S}_n$ be the set of permutations of $[n]=\{1,2,\ldots,n\}$, and let $\mathfrak{S}_n(P_1,\ldots,P_r)$ denote the permutations avoiding the patterns $P_1,\ldots,P_r$. Let A212198 denote the integer sequence referenced in the paper. **The A212198 enumeration conjecture.** The following 13 classes are enumerated by A212198:

$$
\begin{aligned}
&\mathfrak{S}_n(45312,45321,54312,54321),\\
&\mathfrak{S}_n(31245,32145,31254,32154),\\
&\mathfrak{S}_n(31425,32415,31524,32514),\\
&\mathfrak{S}_n(41325,51324,42315,52314),\\
&\mathfrak{S}_n(13425,23415,13524,23514),\\
&\mathfrak{S}_n(13452,23451,13542,23541),\\
&\mathfrak{S}_n(24513,25413,24531,25431),\\
&\mathfrak{S}_n(13245,23145,13254,23154),\\
&\mathfrak{S}_n(32415,34215,32451,34251),\\
&\mathfrak{S}_n(21345,23145,23154,21354),\\
&\mathfrak{S}_n(24135,25134,25314,24315),\\
&\mathfrak{S}_n(42513,52413,42531,52431),\\
&\mathfrak{S}_n(42135,52134,52314,42315).

$$

The first four classes are already established in the paper to have the A212198 enumeration; the remaining nine are presented as conjectured classes in the final remarks. Thus the full 13-class assertion remains open as stated.

349641.title: The entropic-time conjecture for $L_2$ cutoff on random Cayley graphs
349641.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite group and let $G_k$ be its random Cayley graph. For ${L}\in\mathbb{Z}\cup\{\infty\}$, let $\mathbb{Z}_{L}$ denote the cyclic group of order $L$, with $\mathbb{Z}_{\infty}=\mathbb{Z}$, and let $\tilde t_L^\pm(k,G)$ be the time $t$ at which the return probability of the random walk on $\mathbb{Z}_{L}^k$ at time $2t$ equals $|G|^{-1}$. Set

$$
\tilde t_*^\pm(k,G)=\max_{L\in\mathbb{N}}\tilde t_L^\pm(k,G).
$$

**The entropic-time conjecture.** Under conditions similar to those in the paper's total-variation cutoff result, with high probability the random walk on $G_k$ exhibits cutoff in the $L_2$ metric at time $\tilde t_*^\pm(k,G)$. This would identify the $L_2$ cutoff scale through return probabilities on the comparison walks on $\mathbb{Z}_L^k$. The statement is presented informally and the precise conditions are deferred to the cited total-variation result; the paper proves related refined comparisons but does not establish this conjecture in full.
349641.exact_gap_or_exclusion: Literal defers precise hypotheses to total-variation theorem. Uniform group/generator growth conditions and comparison-return optimization unread; no L2 cutoff/concentration argument.

350008.title: Aboulker et al.'s conjecture for out-stars and the directed triangle
350008.statement:
Let $\accentset{\leftrightarrow}{K}_2$ be the complete digraph on two vertices, let $S_2^+$ be the orientation of a two-leaf star with all arcs directed outwards, and let $\vec{C}_3$ be the directed cycle on three vertices. For a family of forbidden induced digraphs, write $\operatorname{Forb}_{\operatorname{ind}}(\cdot)$ for the corresponding class and $\vec{\chi}$ for dichromatic number. **Aboulker et al.'s conjecture.** The two forbidden-subdigraph classes satisfy 
$$
\vec{\chi}(\operatorname{Forb}_{\operatorname{ind}}(\accentset{\leftrightarrow}{K}_2,S_2^+,\vec{C}_3))=\vec{\chi}(\operatorname{Forb}_{\operatorname{ind}}(\accentset{\leftrightarrow}{K}_2,S_2^-,\vec{C}_3))=2.
$$
 The source states that this was open for the two orientations of the three-vertex star, while the paper's conclusion says that it resolves this conjecture; hence its status is recorded as solved.

350055.title: Inverse conjecture for the directional uniformity norms
350055.statement:
Let $p$ be a fixed prime. Suppose that $G$ is a finite-dimensional vector space over the field $\mathbb{F}_p$ with subgroups $H_1, \dots, H_r$. Let $\mathbb{D}=\{z\in\mathbb{C}:|z|\leq 1\}$. Write $\Sigma=\Sigma(H_1,\dots,H_r)$ for the subgroups of $G$ that can be obtained as sums $H_{i_1}+\cdots+H_{i_s}$ for indices $i_1,\dots,i_s\in[r]$ and $s\geq1$, and, for each $K\in\Sigma$, let $d(K)$ be the number of the subgroups $H_i$ contained in $K$. A function on a coset of $K$ is a **non-classical polynomial of degree at most $d(K)-1$** if it is a non-classical polynomial of that degree on the corresponding affine copy of $K$.

**Inverse conjecture for the directional uniformity norms.** If $f\colon G\to\mathbb{D}$ satisfies $\|f\|_{\mathsf{U}(H_1,\dots,H_r)}\geq c$, then there exist functions $u_K\colon G\to\mathbb{F}_p$, for $K\in\Sigma$, such that each $u_K$ is a non-classical polynomial of degree at most $d(K)-1$ on every coset of $K$ in $G$ and

$$
\left|\mathbb{E}_{x\in G} f(x)\prod_{K\in\Sigma}u_K(x)\right|\geq\Omega_{p,c,r}(1).
$$

This conjecture proposes an inverse theorem for directional Gowers uniformity norms over finite vector spaces, extending the classical and box-norm settings. The source states that inverse theorems were then available for classical norms and box norms, while the directional case was being formulated as a conjecture; it is motivated in part by Austin's description of the extremal case.
350055.exact_gap_or_exclusion: Finite-field-valued u_K are multiplied with complex f in a way requiring a source-defined phase embedding; primary directional norms and nonclassical degrees unread. No credit for repairing types or trivial subgroup cases.

350180.title: Baril and Kirgizov's equidistribution conjecture for descent and excedance bistatistics
350180.statement:
Let $cmathfrak{S}_n$ be the symmetric group on $n$ elements. A **bistatistic** is an ordered pair of permutation statistics, and two bistatistics are **equidistributed** if they have the same value distribution on $cmathfrakak{S}_n$. The statistics $\operatorname{des}_2$ and $\operatorname{pex}$ denote, respectively, descents of type $2$ and pure excedances, while $\operatorname{cyc}$ denotes the number of cycles.

**Baril and Kirgizov's conjecture.** The two bistatistics $(\operatorname{des}_2,\operatorname{cyc})$ and $(\operatorname{pex},\operatorname{cyc})$ are equidistributed on $cmathfrak{S}_n$.

Baril and Kirgizov proved the equidistribution of the individual statistics $\operatorname{des}_2$, $\operatorname{pex}$, and $\operatorname{pcyc}$; this conjecture asks for the corresponding joint equidistribution with the cycle statistic.

350272.title: Strong equivariant log-concavity conjecture for Orlik–Solomon algebras
350272.statement:
Let $M$ be a matroid of positive rank, and let $\Gamma$ be a group acting on its ground set while preserving the collection of independent sets. Let $A(M)$ be the **Orlik–Solomon algebra**, defined as the quotient of the exterior algebra on generators indexed by the ground set, and let $B(M)$ be the **reduced Orlik–Solomon algebra**, the subalgebra generated by differences of those generators. A graded representation is strongly equivariantly log concave when its graded tensor products satisfy the subrepresentation inclusions defined in the paper.

**Orlik–Solomon strong log-concavity conjecture.** The Orlik–Solomon algebra $A(M)$ and the reduced Orlik–Solomon algebra $B(M)$ are strongly equivariantly log concave.

When $\Gamma$ is trivial, this reduces to the known log-concavity theorem for characteristic and reduced characteristic polynomials. The equivariant statement for $A(M)$ was previously conjectured and is known for uniform matroids with the full permutation group; the general assertion, including $B(M)$, remains open.
350272.exact_gap_or_exclusion: Need actual representation subobject ordering and all matroid/group cases; trivial-group characteristic polynomial logconcavity is not the equivariant claim. No all-rank representation injection.

350325.title: Hodges and Yong's maximal sphericity conjecture for Schubert varieties
350325.statement: Let $G/B$ be a flag variety, let $w\in S_n$ index the Schubert variety $X_w\subseteq G/B$, and let $J(w)$ be the left descent set of $w$. Write $P_{J(w)}$ for the corresponding parabolic subgroup and $L_{J(w)}$ for its Levi subgroup. The variety $X_w$ is **maximally spherical** if it is $L_{J(w)}$-spherical for the induced action, equivalently if a Borel subgroup of $L_{J(w)}$ has a dense orbit in $X_w$. A permutation $w$ is **spherical** if it has a reduced word satisfying conditions (S.1) and (S.2) in the source definition. **Hodges and Yong's conjecture.** The Schubert variety $X_w$ is maximally spherical if and only if $w$ is spherical. This geometric characterization is part of the connection between spherical Schubert varieties and permutation pattern avoidance; the claim is stated as proven in forthcoming work of Gao--Hodges--Yong.

351028.title: Cylindric Naruse hook-length formula
351028.statement:
Let $m,\ell \in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 1}$ and let $\lambda,\mu \in \mathcal{P}_{m,\ell}$ satisfy $\lambda \supset \mu$. Put

$$
n=|\lambda/\mu|=|\mathring{\lambda}/\mathring{\mu}|.
$$

Here $f^{\mathring{\lambda}/\mathring{\mu}}$ denotes the number of linear extensions of the cylindric skew diagram, $\mathcal{E}_{\mathring{\lambda}}(\mathring{\mu})$ is the set of cylindric excited diagrams of $\mathring{\mu}$ in $\mathring{\lambda}$, and $h_{\mathring{\lambda}}(x)$ is the hook length of $x$ in $\mathring{\lambda}$. **Cylindric Naruse hook-length formula.**

$$
f^{\mathring{\lambda}/\mathring{\mu}}=n!\sum_{D\in\mathcal{E}_{\mathring{\lambda}}(\mathring{\mu})}\prod_{x\in\mathring{\lambda}\setminus D}\frac{1}{h_{\mathring{\lambda}}(x)}.
$$

This is the cylindric analogue of Naruse's hook-length formula for ordinary skew diagrams, expressing the number of linear extensions through cylindric excited diagrams and hook lengths.
351028.exact_gap_or_exclusion: Cylindric excited diagrams, hook lengths, admissible partitions and winding cases unread; ordinary Naruse formula does not directly establish cylindric version.

351165.title: Sharper Randić index–diameter ratio conjecture for cactus graphs
351165.statement:
Let $G$ be a cactus with $k$ cycles and $b$ bridges; write $n$ for its number of vertices, $R$ for its Randić index, and $d$ for its diameter. A **BC-tree** is the block-cut tree of $G$, and a graph is **longitudinally symmetric** when it has the symmetry specified by the paper. **Cactus diameter-ratio conjecture.** For a nontrivial cactus ($b=0$),

$$
\frac{R}{d}\geq \frac{n-(k-1)(3-2\sqrt 2)}{n+k-1},
$$

with equality if the BC-tree is a path and is longitudinally symmetric. For a cactus with $k>0$ and $b>0$,

$$
\frac{R}{d}\geq \frac{n-(k-1)(3-2\sqrt 2)-6+\frac{4}{\sqrt 3}+4\sqrt{\frac{2}{3}}}{n+k+b-1},
$$

with equality if the BC-tree is a path, the graph has two leaves, and it is longitudinally symmetric. This is proposed as a sharper diameter-ratio bound incorporating cycles and bridges; the supplied text says it is proved only for cacti whose BC-tree is starlike.
351165.exact_gap_or_exclusion: Both numerical inequalities proved in SUSTAINED-ORDINARY-ROUTES.md. Equality term longitudinally symmetric not precisely defined and mixed two-leaf vs two-pendant-bridge mismatch unpaid. No full-literal survivor.

351197.title: Hu–Ye's geometric-versus-algebraic nullity conjecture for hypermatrices
351197.statement:
Let $M$ be an order-$k$ hypermatrix, let $\operatorname{am}(\lambda)$ be the algebraic multiplicity of $\lambda$ as an eigenvalue of $M$, and let $V_\lambda^1,\ldots,V_\lambda^\kappa$ be the irreducible components of the eigenvariety $V_\lambda$ corresponding to $\lambda$. Define

$$
\operatorname{gm}(\lambda):=\sum_{j=1}^\kappa \dim(V_\lambda^j)(k-1)^{\dim(V_\lambda^j)-1}.
$$

**Hu–Ye's conjecture.** For any order-$k$ hypermatrix $M$,

$$
\operatorname{gm}(\lambda)\leq\operatorname{am}(\lambda).
$$

This conjecture seeks to generalize the fact that the geometric multiplicity of a matrix eigenvalue is bounded above by its algebraic multiplicity, with the eigenvariety playing the role of the geometric eigenspace for hypermatrices. The relationship between these quantities is described in the source as almost entirely unexplored for hypergraphs.
351197.exact_gap_or_exclusion: Need exact resultant/eigenvariety multiplicity conventions, origin/zero-dimensional components and all nonsymmetric tensor cases. Component dimension inequality not a multiplicity proof; no mechanism.

351851.title: Conjecture on rank-one solutions for edge sums in the max-cut SDP
351851.statement:
Let $G_1$ and $G_2$ be two graphs with vertex sets

$$
V_1=\{1,2,\ldots,m+1,m+2\},\qquad V_2=\{m+1,m+2,\ldots,n-1,n\}.
$$

Let $(X_1,S_1)$ and $(X_2,S_2)$ be the primal-dual solution pairs to the max-cut SDPs on $G_1$ and $G_2$, respectively. Let $G$ be the edge sum of $G_1$ and $G_2$, with common edge $(m+1,m+2)$, and let $(X^*,S^*)$ be the primal and dual optimal solutions for $G$. **Edge-sum conjecture.** The following statements are equivalent: (1) $X_1$ and $X_2$ are rank-one matrices and agree on the intersection; (2) for some common choice of signs on the off-diagonal $w_1$ entries, the dual solution has the form

$$
S=\begin{bmatrix} S_1^* & 0 \\ 0 & 0 \end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix} 0 & 0 \\ 0 & S_2^* \end{bmatrix}-\frac14\begin{bmatrix} 0&0&0&0\\0&w_1&\pm w_1&0\\0&\pm w_1&w_1&0\\0&0&0&0\end{bmatrix}.
$$

The first two matrices are $n\times n$; $S_1$ is $(m+2)\times(m+2)$ and $S_2$ is $(n-m)\times(n-m)$, while in the final matrix the $w_1$ entries occur in positions $(m+1,m+1)$ and $(m+2,m+2)$ (with the off-diagonal entries carrying the common sign). This conjecture concerns how rank-one primal solutions and the corresponding dual structure behave under an edge sum, extending the paper's results for vertex sums and special edge sums. Its resolution for general edge sums or larger clique sums is left as future work.
351851.exact_gap_or_exclusion: Printed minus-diagonal correction refuted by a personally derived positive-weight two-triangle family. Complete Definitions1/2+slack bridge and source Theorem4 show a source sign correction, zero credit.

352188.title: Principal representation conjecture for normal homogeneous subrings of graphs
352188.statement:
Let $G$ be an unmixed graph, let $S$ be its homogeneous subring, and let $B$ be the configuration defining $S$. Write $(\mathbb{R}_+B)^\circ$ for the relative interior of the cone generated by $B$, and call a representation of $w\in\mathbb{N}B$ **principal** when it has the principal form defined for the configuration $B$. A **strong $\lceil\frac{n}{2}\rceil$-$\tau$-reduction** is a reduction of $G$ with the stated strength. **Principal representation conjecture.** If $S$ is normal and $G$ is unmixed with a strong $\lceil\frac{n}{2}\rceil$-$\tau$-reduction, then every

$$
w\in(\mathbb{R}_+B)^\circ\cap\mathbb{N}B
$$

has a principal representation. This representation property is intended to support the characterization of when the normal homogeneous subring $S$ is Gorenstein; the paper subsequently uses it to establish the corresponding implication, while the conjectural equivalence itself is the broader claim left for verification.

352547.title: The consistency and perfect-matching conjecture for brane tilings
352547.statement:
Let a brane tiling have a corresponding toric diagram, either reflexive or non-reflexive. For each boundary point of the toric diagram, consider the coefficient of the associated Newton polynomial and its maximally tempered value, and let perfect matchings be the combinatorial objects associated to the tiling.

**Consistency and perfect-matching conjecture.** A brane tiling is consistent if and only if the corresponding toric diagram has maximally tempered coefficients for its boundary points. Moreover, the maximally tempered coefficients are equal to the numbers of perfect matchings associated to the boundary points.

This conjecture seeks a common characterization of consistency, Newton-polynomial coefficients, and perfect-matchings data for reflexive and non-reflexive toric diagrams. The paper presents the claim as a natural conjecture based on the examples discussed.
352547.exact_gap_or_exclusion: Consistency, maximally tempered coefficients, gauge normalization and boundary matchings need primary definitions. No all-reflexive/nonreflexive tiling mechanism.

352883.title: The major-index polynomial-degree conjecture
352883.statement:
Let $S_n$ be the symmetric group, let $\operatorname{maj}(\pi)$ denote the major index of $\pi$, and let $M(n,k)$ be the number of permutations $w\in S_n$ with $\operatorname{inv}(w)=k$. For fixed $k>0$ and $n\geq k$, consider the expected value of the first letter conditioned on $\operatorname{maj}(\pi)=k$.

**Major-index conjecture.** This expected value is a rational function in $n$ that is $1/(k+1)$ times the quotient of a monic degree-$(k+1)$ polynomial by a monic degree-$k$ polynomial. In particular, the source gives

$$
\mathbb{E}[\pi(1)\mid \pi\in S_n,\operatorname{maj}(\pi)=1]=\frac{1}{2}\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\originalleft(\frac{n^2+n-2}{n-1}\aftergroup\egroup\originalright),
$$

$$
\mathbb{E}[\pi(1)\mid \pi\in S_n,\operatorname{maj}(\pi)=2]=\frac{1}{3}\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\originalleft(\frac{n^3-n-6}{n^2-n-2}\aftergroup\egroup\originalright),
$$

$$
\mathbb{E}[\pi(1)\mid \pi\in S_n,\operatorname{maj}(\pi)=3]=\frac{1}{4}\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\originalleft(\frac{n^4+6n^3-13n^2-18n}{n^3-7n}\aftergroup\egroup\originalright),
$$

$$
\mathbb{E}[\pi(1)\mid \pi\in S_n,\operatorname{maj}(\pi)=4]=\frac{1}{5}\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\originalleft(\frac{n^5+20n^4-45n^3-80n^2-16n}{n^4+2n^3-13n^2-14n}\aftergroup\egroup\originalright).
$$

The denominator is an integer multiple of $M(n,k)$, a degree-$k$ polynomial. This is presented as a conjectured pattern for the major index; the supplied text gives no resolution evidence, so it remains open.
352883.exact_gap_or_exclusion: Full ordinary descent-set proof is already public in actual issue19720 body, creation reported2026-10-21; exact all-parameter bridge read. Excluded public proof; empty fibers are source endpoint defects.

345544.title: The extremal degree conjecture for eventually constant 0-Hecke operators
345544.statement:
Let $S_n$ be the symmetric group, let $t_i:S_n\to S_n$ be the adjacent sorting operators, and let $H_0(S_n)=\langle t_1,\ldots,t_{n-1}\rangle$ be the $0$-Hecke monoid. An element $T\in H_0(S_n)$ is **eventually constant** if some positive power $T^k$ is the constant map with value $123\cdots n$. Let ${\bf B}:S_n\to S_n$ be bubble sort. Define $T_{\operatorname{odd}}$ and $T_{\operatorname{even}}$ by applying, respectively, the odd- and even-indexed operators in increasing order, and set $T_{\operatorname{tla}}=T_{\operatorname{odd}}\circ T_{\operatorname{even}}$.

**Extremal degree conjecture.** If $T\in H_0(S_n)$ is eventually constant, then

$$
\deg({\bf B}:S_n\to S_n)\leq\deg(T:S_n\to S_n)\leq\deg(T_{\operatorname{tla}}:S_n\to S_n).
$$

The conjecture asserts that bubble sort is closest to invertible and $T_{\operatorname{tla}}$ is farthest among eventually constant elements. The lower bound is explicit, since $\deg({\bf B}:S_n\to S_n)=n(n+1)/6$, while the paper says that the upper extremal degree is unknown; both inequalities remain open.

345740.title: Coefficient bounds conjecture for Ehrhart polynomials of connected matroids
345740.statement:
Let $M$ be a connected matroid of rank $k$ on $n$ elements. Write $i(M,t)$ for its Ehrhart polynomial, and let $T_{k,n}$ and $U_{k,n}$ denote respectively the minimal and uniform matroids of rank $k$ on $n$ elements. For polynomials $P(t)$ and $Q(t)$, write $P(t)\preceq Q(t)$ when every coefficient of $P$ is at most the corresponding coefficient of $Q$. **Coefficient bounds conjecture.**

$$
i(T_{k,n},t)\preceq i(M,t)\preceq i(U_{k,n},t).
$$

This conjecture asks whether the minimal and uniform matroids give coefficientwise lower and upper bounds among connected matroids with fixed rank and cardinality. The containment of matroid polytopes in the corresponding hypersimplex gives the point-counting inequality, but coefficientwise bounds for the Ehrhart polynomials remain open in the supplied context.

345791.title: The functional isometric-tripling conjecture
345791.statement:
For a nonnegative function $f\in\ell^1(G)$, define its unrestricted, isometric, and isomeric functional triplings by

$$
\gamma(f)=\inf_{g,h}\frac{\lVert f\mathbin{\overline *}g\mathbin{\overline *}h\rVert_1}{\lVert g\rVert_2\lVert h\rVert_2},
$$

$$
\gamma'(f)=\inf_{g\sim h}\frac{\lVert f\mathbin{\overline *}g\mathbin{\overline *}h\rVert_1}{\lVert g\rVert_2\lVert h\rVert_2},\qquad
\gamma”(f)=\inf_g\frac{\lVert f\mathbin{\overline *}g\mathbin{\overline *}g\rVert_1}{\lVert g\rVert_2^2},
$$

where $\overline *$ is max-convolution and $g\sim h$ means that $g$ and $h$ have the same distribution function.

**Functional isometric-tripling conjecture.**

$$
\gamma=\gamma'=\gamma”.
$$

The conjecture asks whether the unrestricted, isometric, and isomeric functional triplings coincide. It is the functional analogue of the proposed equality among the corresponding set-based parameters.
345791.exact_gap_or_exclusion: Source siblings345784/345785 concern log-span and linear-matroid induced tripling, not equality of these functional infima. Need group, admissible g,h, nonzero denominator and distribution definitions; symmetrization might change max convolution.

346154.title: Finiteness conjecture for restricted-digit additive triples
346154.statement:
Let $b\geq 3$ be an integer, and let $B_b$ denote the set of positive integers whose base-$b$ expansion contains only the digits $0$ and $1$. Let $a,b,c\geq 3$ be pairwise multiplicatively independent integers, meaning that $\log a/\log b$, $\log a/\log c$, and $\log b/\log c$ are irrational. **Restricted-digit additive-triples conjecture.** If

$$
\frac{\log 2}{\log a}+\frac{\log 2}{\log b}+\frac{\log 2}{\log c}<1,
$$

then there are only finitely many integers $(x,y,z)\in B_a\times B_b\times B_c$ such that

$$
x+y=z.
$$

The conjecture predicts finiteness in the dimension-sum-below-one regime. The paper presents it as a suspected consequence of the thinness of the restricted-digit sets; related results establish strong upper bounds, but the asserted finiteness is not supplied as a theorem here.
346154.exact_gap_or_exclusion: Pairwise multiplicative independence/dimension sum read. Thin-set dimension heuristics do not prove finite intersections with x+y=z; no infinite-scale Diophantine mechanism.

347236.title: The capacity formula conjecture for strictly positive channels
347236.statement:
Let $P_{Z|X}$ be a strictly positive discrete memoryless channel (DMC), let $\hat{P}_{X_1^n}$ and $\hat{P}_{Y_1^n}$ denote the empirical distributions of the input and output sequences, and let $\mathcal{P}_{\mathcal{X}^n}$ denote the set of probability distributions on $\mathcal{X}^n$. Write $\operatorname{rank}(P_{Z|X})$ for the rank of the channel matrix. **Capacity formula conjecture.** For any strictly positive DMC $P_{Z|X}$,

$$
C_{\mathsf{perm}}(P_{Z|X})=\liminf_{n\rightarrow\infty}\frac{1}{\log(n)}\sup_{P_{X_1^n}\in\mathcal{P}_{\mathcal{X}^n}} I(\hat{P}_{X_1^n};\hat{P}_{Y_1^n})=\frac{\operatorname{rank}(P_{Z|X})-1}{2},
$$

where the supremum is over all probability distributions in $\mathcal{P}_{\mathcal{X}^n}$, or equivalently over all probability distributions of $\hat{P}_{X_1^n}$. This would extend the paper's closed-form capacity result from strictly positive full-rank DMCs to general strictly positive DMCs; its resolution is not established here.
347236.exact_gap_or_exclusion: Source sibling347237 BEC literal-only prior is distinct and not strictly positive. Need exact channel coding definition, rank-deficient converse and uniform information asymptotics; no ordinary capacity proof.
